references.text: Miriam and the women went out with drums and dancing to celebrate the victory, just as Jephthah's daughter went out to meet her father with drums and dancing.
The women came out from all the towns of Israel with singing and dancing, with drums and musical instruments, to celebrate David's victory, just as Jephthah's daughter met her father.
Isaac was Abraham's only son through Sarah, just as Jephthah's daughter was his only child. Both stories are about a father who must sacrifice his only child.
Jephthah's vow that led to his daughter coming out to meet him. This is the context for the daughter going out with drums and dancing.
The continuation of the story of Jephthah's daughter, describing the consequences of her being the first to meet him.
Young women playing drums in processions, which recalls Jephthah's daughter who came out with drums.
Praise with dancing and drumming, just as Jephthah's daughter used drums and dancing.
Praise with drum and dance, reflecting the traditional way of celebrating victory that Jephthah's daughter demonstrated.
